newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March S&P 500s close lower, diverge from Dow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March S&P 500s close lower, diverge from Dow.

text.p: U.S. March Standard & Poor's 500 futures closed lower, diverging from the Dow Jones Industrial Average, as the overall market remained extremely volatile, traders and analysts said.
"Volatility was off the charts, so it doesn't take much to move the market," one floor trader said about March S&Ps' sudden plunge into negative territory.
March S&Ps held tentative gains before midday, but decisively erased gains and turned lower in line with U.S. bonds. Some traders said S&Ps were attempting to correct overbought gains from Friday.

On the other hand, the Dow Industrials were recouping losses from Friday, leading the index in an opposite direction from S&Ps for part of the day. The Dow closed 23 points higher at 6,567, its first record close of 1997.
Nikkei 225 contracts also finished higher after March extended gains above the 19,500 level.
Light buying from one major U.S. retail house lifted March S&Ps off their session low 749.10, which was set quickly on heavy sell-stop orders, traders said.
"Everyone was off kilter because there weren't any reports or news out," one trader said.
Several traders described the sell-off as technical, as March broke below a rolling pivot area of 754.00 to 754.20.
"That was the turning point," another floor trader said.
Arbitrage sell programs were also noted when March narrowed its premium to cash to about 4.90 points, they said.
One U.S. institution sold about 1,200 contracts, while another U.S. firm that reportedly was a heavy buyer late Friday and an intermittent buyer early Monday sold about 600 contracts late in the day.

At the end of pit trade, March S&P 500s were down 6.50 at 750.70, New Composites were down 2.55 at 396.20, Nikkeis were 190 higher at 19,505, KCBT Value Lines were down 3.70 at 689.00, Midcap 400s were down 0.40 at 259.10 and Nasdaq 100s were up 1.25 at 860.00. ((--Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750))
